I need a precise, evidence-grounded accounting of the CodeRabbit review comment situation on the open PR for this branch.

Steps:
1. Find the PR: `gh pr list --head feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui --state all --json number,title,url,createdAt,updatedAt`. Also try `gh pr view --json number,title,url,createdAt,reviewDecision`.
2. Get ALL review comments (inline/thread comments) on that PR, with author, created date, and whether the thread has a reply. Use the GraphQL API for thread resolution status, e.g.:
   `gh api graphql -f query='query { repository(owner:"ZimmermannAU", name:"zimmermann-pwa") { pullRequest(number: N) { reviewThreads(first:100) { nodes { isResolved isOutdated comments(first:20) { nodes { author { login } createdAt body } } } } } } }'`
   (substitute the real PR number). If the owner is different, get it from `gh repo view --json owner,name`.
3. Count precisely:
   - total review threads authored by CodeRabbit (coderabbitai)
   - how many have ZERO human/author reply in-thread (i.e. only coderabbit comments in the thread)
   - how many are resolved vs unresolved
   - the createdAt date of the OLDEST unanswered CodeRabbit thread, and the newest
4. Also list top-level PR review submissions (`gh pr view N --json reviews`) with dates, and issue comments (`gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/issues/N/comments`) to see if replies were posted as separate top-level comments rather than in-thread.
5. For each unanswered thread, give a ONE-LINE summary of what CodeRabbit flagged (file + gist), so I can judge severity.

Context on why this matters: this project's AGENTS.md mandates "always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every finding, whether it's fixed or not" because CodeRabbit's learning feature picks up patterns from PR conversation. So unanswered threads are a documented process violation, not just a nicety. Note whether replies exist anywhere at all.

If gh is not authenticated or the API is unavailable, say so explicitly rather than guessing. Report exact counts and dates. Include the PR number and URL.
